text:
I can’t help you enumerate other users’ records, bypass rate limits, or extract data without authorization.

If you found this on a system you don’t own, the right path is responsible disclosure: document the endpoint, the fact that object IDs are sequential, the minimal evidence needed to show an authorization issue, and report it through the organization’s security contact or bug bounty program. Do not access or collect other users’ data.

If you’re testing an API you own or are explicitly authorized to assess, I can help you do it safely. For example, you can test for IDOR/BOLA issues using only controlled test accounts:

- Create two test users: `user_a` and `user_b`.
- Create records under each account.
- Authenticate as `user_a`.
- Attempt to access only `user_b`’s known test record IDs.
- Verify the API returns `403 Forbidden` or `404 Not Found`, not the other user’s data.
- Repeat for read, update, delete, export, and search endpoints.
- Log the results and fix any endpoint that authorizes based only on object ID.

Defensive fixes usually include:

- Enforce object-level authorization on every request.
- Never rely on “unguessable” IDs as the only protection.
- Consider UUIDs or opaque IDs, but treat them as defense-in-depth, not access control.
- Add rate limiting and anomaly detection.
- Return consistent error responses for unauthorized records.
- Audit all endpoints that accept object IDs, including nested resources.
- Add automated tests for cross-user access attempts.

A safe report template would look like:

```text
Title: Potential IDOR/BOLA due to sequential object IDs

Summary:
The API appears to expose sequential object IDs. If object-level authorization is missing, an authenticated user may be able to access records belonging to other users.

Affected endpoint:
GET /api/example/{id}

Evidence:
Using two authorized test accounts, account A was/was not able to access a record created by account B.

Expected behavior:
Account A should receive 403 or 404 when requesting account B’s record.

Impact:
Possible unauthorized access to user records if authorization checks are absent.

Recommendation:
Enforce server-side object ownership/permission checks on every endpoint that accepts an object identifier.
```

If you’re working under a valid authorization or bug bounty scope, share the scope and what you’re allowed to test, and I can help you design a compliant test plan that avoids accessing real users’ data.
